# Dokkit

> Self-hosted monitoring that says what needs a look. A server you host, one small program on each machine, and one API behind everything.

An AI tool reaches Dokkit over MCP at `/mcp` on the server, or over the HTTP API, with a user token whose scopes decide what it may do.

## Docs

- [The API](https://dokkit.dev/api.md): every call, with what to send and what comes back
- [The command line](https://dokkit.dev/cli.md): every `dokkit` command
- [The API as OpenAPI 3.1](https://dokkit.dev/openapi.json)
- [Everything in one file](https://dokkit.dev/llms-full.txt): the API, the command line, the MCP tools and the `dokkit.toml` reference


# The MCP server

Dokkit serves a Model Context Protocol endpoint at `/mcp` so an AI tool can ask it questions and act, as far as its token allows.

It lives on the server, never on `dokkit`. It is a client of the same API and uses a user token, so it can never do more than that token allows.

## Connecting

Over HTTP with a user token as a bearer header. For Claude Code:

```
claude mcp add --transport http dokkit https://<dokkit address>/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer dku_..."
```

## Tools

| Tool | Scope | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `attention` | `read` | Shows what needs a look now, what will soon, what was found and is not watched, what is snoozed, issues in other environments, and how many things are fine. |
| `find` | `read` | Searches services, optionally on one machine. |
| `service` | `read` | Shows one service: state, checks, routing, open issue. |
| `since_deploy` | `read` | Shows what changed or broke for a service since its last deploy. |
| `jobs` | `read` | Lists jobs with their schedule and last runs. |
| `job_runs` | `read` | Lists the recent runs of one job. |
| `errors` | `read` | Lists error groups, or shows one with its stack. |
| `tasks` | `read` | Lists the accepted tasks. |
| `task_runs` | `read` | Lists the recent runs of every task. |
| `machines` | `read` | Lists machines. |
| `machine` | `read` | Shows one machine. |
| `issues` | `read` | Lists issues. |
| `issue` | `read` | Shows one issue with its history. |
| `deploys` | `read` | Lists recent deploys. |
| `versions` | `read` | Lists the versions of the apps Dokkit watches. |
| `rules` | `read` | Lists the alert rules. |
| `proposals` | `read` | Lists what Dokkit found and a person may accept or dismiss. |
| `series` | `read` | Shows numbers over time for a service. |
| `day` | `read` | Shows the last 24 hours in half hours: for each machine whether something was down, needed a look, or nothing happened, or it was not heard from, and the issues that opened. |
| `alert_settings` | `read` | Shows the alert settings. Addresses, user names and secrets are only `set` or `not set`. |
| `alert_suggestions` | `read` | Lists issues that keep opening, which the daily digest could take instead. |
| `logs` | `read-logs` | Searches log lines. |
| `archives` | `read-logs` | Lists the archived months of logs that can be loaded back. |
| `snooze` | `act` | Snoozes an issue until a time. |
| `unsnooze` | `act` | Wakes a snoozed issue. |
| `acknowledge` | `act` | Marks an issue as seen. |
| `note` | `act` | Adds a note to an issue. |
| `bulk` | `act` | Snoozes, unsnoozes or acknowledges many issues. |
| `watch` | `act` | Starts watching a service. |
| `unwatch` | `act` | Stops watching a service. |
| `routing` | `act` | Sets where a service's issues go. A field that is not given stays as it was. |
| `hold` | `act` | Holds a service at a version. |
| `accept_proposal` | `act` | Accepts a found service or port. A task is accepted with `accept_task`. |
| `dismiss_proposal` | `act` | Dismisses a proposal. |
| `run_task` | `act` | Runs an accepted task. |
| `keep_messages` | `act` | Keeps or stops keeping the text of a service's errors. |
| `set_job_timing` | `act` | Sets when a job counts as late and as run too long. A field left out stays as it was; an empty one clears it. |
| `add_rule` | `admin` | Adds an alert rule. |
| `update_rule` | `admin` | Changes an alert rule. A field left out stays as it was; an empty one clears it. |
| `delete_rule` | `admin` | Deletes an alert rule. |
| `set_checks` | `admin` | Replaces the checks added in the interface. |
| `allow_restart` | `admin` | Allows or forbids restarting a service. |
| `keys` | `admin` | Lists keys and tokens, never their text. |
| `make_key` | `admin` | Makes a key. Its text is returned once. |
| `revoke_key` | `admin` | Revokes a key. |
| `people` | `admin` | Lists the people who can sign in. |
| `add_person` | `admin` | Adds a person. |
| `remove_person` | `admin` | Removes a person. |
| `accept_task` | `admin` | Accepts a waiting task, so its machine may run the command. Takes the command and pin that `proposals` shows. |
| `dismiss_task` | `admin` | Dismisses a waiting task. |
| `update_program` | `admin` | Asks an enrolled machine to fetch the newer `dokkit` program. |
| `add_job` | `admin` | Adds a job to watch. Its key and addresses are returned once. |
| `set_alert_settings` | `admin` | Changes alert settings. A setting left out stays as it was; an empty secret clears it. If the address a secret goes to changes (`ntfy_url`, `smtp_host`), send the secret again in the same call or it is cleared, and the answer says so. |
| `test_alert` | `admin` | Sends a test alert by one channel. Answers sent, or one fixed reason. Four at once for each token, then one every 25 seconds. |
| `accept_suggestion` | `admin` | Sends a service's issues to the daily digest from now on. |
| `dismiss_suggestion` | `admin` | Dismisses an alert suggestion. |
| `restore_archive` | `admin` | Loads an archived month of logs back for a week. |

## Rules

- **Log contents have their own scope.** A token can be given everything except what is written in the logs.
- **A new token has no `act` scope** unless it is asked for.
- **Read tools are marked read-only**, so a client can run them without asking each time. `admin` tools are marked destructive.
- **What comes back is data.** Names, titles, notes, error text, deploy fields and output were written by machines and apps. Every answer starts with a line that says so.
- **Arguments are checked against the types the tool declares.** A wrong type is an `isError` answer, not a failure. A `null` argument is the same as one left out, and a whole number written as `5.0` is an integer. To clear a route, send an empty text.
- **A token with `admin` can do through MCP everything a person can do in the interface.** Making such a token asks for confirmation in Settings.

## Built so far

`POST /mcp` with a user token: every tool in the table, 57 in all (21 `read`, 2 `read-logs`, 14 `act`, 20 `admin`), one for each call of the API a token can make. Making a full-control token and the browser's own sign-in have no tool: they are Settings and the browser only. A tool the token may not use is not listed.


# `dokkit.toml`

One file in an app's repo that says what the app is and how to tell if it is healthy. It ships with the app.

```toml
schema = 1

[service]
id = "upload-portal"
name = "Upload portal"
kind = "service"                # service, job, dependency or app
environment = "production"      # anything else never alerts
version_from = "stats"          # "stats", a file path, or a command

[[check]]
type = "http"
url = "http://localhost:8080/healthz"
every = "30s"
timeout = "5s"
slow = "2s"                     # an answer slower than this is degraded, not down; http only, above 0, below timeout

[stats]
url = "http://localhost:8080/internal/stats"
key_env = "DOKKIT_STATS_KEY"     # the name of the variable, never the secret; must start with DOKKIT_STATS_

[logs]
path = "logs/*.jsonl"

[[job]]
id = "nightly-purge"
schedule = "0 1 * * *"
grace = "30m"
max_runtime = "1h"

[[task]]
id = "security-scan"
run = "scripts/zap.ps1"
timeout = "2h"                  # the server ends a run still going after 12 hours

[alert]
down = "page"                   # a suggested default only
degraded = "push"
```

## Sections

| Section | Holds |
|---|---|
| `schema` | The version of this file format. `1`. |
| `[service]` | What the app is. `id` is unique on its machine and never changes. |
| `[[check]]` | One per check. `type` is one of the check types in `api.md`. Each type has its own fields: `url` for `http`, `port` for `tcp`, `name` for `process`, `windows-service` and `systemd` (the unit), `metric` and `limit` for `threshold` (bad when the metric is over the limit), `date_from` for `expiry` (an `https` address or `host:port` for a certificate, or a file whose first line is a date). All take `every`. `http` also takes `slow`: an answer that comes back successfully but takes longer is `degraded`, with the time as its value, and the server opens an issue only after its usual run of bad results. |
| `[stats]` | Where the stats document is and which environment variable holds its key. |
| `[logs]` | Files to read. Paths are relative to the file and must stay inside its folder. Lines follow `log-lines.md`. |
| `[[job]]` | A scheduled job: when it should run, how late it may be, and how long it may take. `schedule` is a five-field cron line read as UTC, and `@reboot` is refused. |
| `[[task]]` | A named piece of work the server may be allowed to ask for. |
| `[alert]` | A starting suggestion for who is told. |

## Rules

**The file owns what the app is and how to check it. The interface owns who is told, snoozes and overrides.** The interface shows a file-declared check as coming from the file, and it is changed by changing the file. `[alert]` only seeds the routing the first time the service appears.

**Secrets never go in the file.** A field ending in `_env` names an environment variable that holds one.

**A declared check is active straight away. A declared task is not.** A task is a command that the server could later ask a machine to run. It arrives as a proposal, is accepted in the interface, and is pinned to what was accepted: the exact command, the absolute path of the declaring file and the contents of every word of the command that is a regular file inside the task's folder. If any of them changes, it is proposed again and the old one stops being runnable. A task runs under an ordinary account unless it was accepted to run otherwise. Without this, anyone able to edit a file in a repo could get a command run by a privileged service.

**Tasks take no arguments.** The server can ask for a task by name and nothing else.

## How the file reaches Dokkit

Two ways, both supported:

1. **`dokkit` reads it.** `dokkit`'s own configuration lists the folders it may read `dokkit.toml` files from. That configuration is only editable by an administrator. `dokkit` re-reads a file when it changes.
2. **It is sent.** `dokkit apply` sends the file from anywhere that has a key, for example from CI.

## Checking it

`dokkit check` validates the file, runs every check once on the current machine, and prints exactly what would be sent. It needs no server.


# The `dokkit` command line

One program on each watched machine, also used in an app's repo. `dokkit help` prints this list and `dokkit help <command>` says more about one.


## In an app's repo


### `dokkit init`

Asks what the app is and writes dokkit.toml. Asks a few questions and writes a dokkit.toml in this folder: what the app is, and how to tell it is healthy. Nothing is sent.


### `dokkit check [dokkit.toml]`

Runs the checks it can once and prints what would be sent. Checks the file's schema, service id and each check's fields. Runs the http, tcp, process, windows-service, systemd and expiry checks that can run here, once, and prints exactly what would be sent. Checks the app reports itself are listed as not run. A check aimed at another host does make its request. Needs no server and sends nothing to it. A slow answer shows as slow, not as a failure.


### `dokkit apply [dokkit.toml]`

Sends the file to the server. Declares the file to the server, for a file dokkit watch does not read. It needs this machine's key from dokkit enrol; the server refuses an app key. Sending the same file twice changes nothing.


## Jobs


### `dokkit run [--service <slug>] --job <name> -- <command> [arguments]`

Runs a command and reports how it went. Runs the command and reports its start, finish, exit code, duration and last lines of output. Exits with the command's own exit code. With this machine's key, a job declared in a dokkit.toml in the folders of the saved configuration is found by name, and --service says which service when it is not. With an app key, --service is ignored.


### `dokkit ping [--service <slug>] <name> [start|ok|fail]`

Reports a job that cannot be wrapped. Reports one event for a job: start, ok (the default) or fail.


## This machine


### `dokkit enrol <address> <token> [sha256:<certificate fingerprint>]`

Joins this machine to a server. Trades a one-time token for this machine's key and saves it. Given a fingerprint, it trusts the certificate with that fingerprint and no other.


### `dokkit status`

What this machine watches and when it last reported. Shows the files dokkit watch reads, when it last sent, and how many reports are waiting, and any folder it cannot read. It says a watch is running only while that watch has written down in the last three minutes, and then gives its process number. On Linux it shows the installed service when root, or the dokkit group, can read its files; the service's status itself can be read only with sudo.


### `dokkit doctor`

A rough check of the server and the clock. Says whether the server answers and knows this key, whether this machine's clock is within 30 seconds of the server's (a slow answer counts as clock difference, up to 10 seconds), and whether reports are waiting. A certificate that is not the one saved at enrol shows as the server not answering.


## Finding things


### `dokkit scan [--no-services] [--no-ports] [--no-tasks] [--no-containers] [--no-sites] [--no-disks] [--no-declarations]`

Looks over this machine and writes a proposal file. Lists what is on the machine that could be watched and writes it to dokkit-proposal.json in this folder. Sends nothing. Each --no- flag leaves one kind of thing out.


### `dokkit propose`

Sends the proposal file to be accepted. Sends dokkit-proposal.json, which a scan wrote. Nothing in it is watched until a person accepts it in the interface, or a token allowed to act accepts it through the API.


## Staying running


### `dokkit watch [--background]`

Watches this machine, as an ordinary program. Reads dokkit.toml files from the folders in DOKKIT_FOLDERS or in the saved configuration, and from the folders directly inside them. Runs their checks, sends the log files they name, runs the tasks a person accepted, and says the machine is alive once a minute. No administrator, no service. --background leaves it running after this window closes. Run like this, it never restarts a service or unit; only the installed service does.


### `dokkit folder add|remove <path>`

Sets which folders dokkit watch reads dokkit.toml files from. Adds a folder to the list dokkit watch reads dokkit.toml files from, or takes one out. It reads the dokkit.toml in the folder and in the folders directly inside it. The path is made absolute, and for add the folder must exist. Adding one twice changes nothing. A running watch picks up the change within a minute, with no restart. When the service is installed this changes the service's list, which needs an administrator, or root on Linux, and it prints the exact line to run. Otherwise it changes your own list. On Linux, it warns when the dokkit user cannot read the folder.


### `dokkit folder list`

Shows those folders. Lists the folders dokkit watch reads dokkit.toml files from: the installed service's when there is one, otherwise your own, and any it cannot read.


### `dokkit startup on|off`

Starts dokkit watch each time you sign in. Windows only. Works on Windows only so far. Adds dokkit watch --background to your own startup programs, or takes it out. No administrator. On Linux, use dokkit service, or add dokkit watch --background to your desktop's startup programs. On macOS, add it to a launchd job.


### `dokkit service install|uninstall|update|start|stop`

Runs it as a service, on Windows or Linux. Needs an administrator or root. Works on Windows and on Linux with systemd; not on macOS yet. Installs dokkit as a service that starts with the machine, so it keeps watching with nobody signed in. On Windows it runs as Local Service, an account with no rights of its own, and reads only what that account can read, which leaves out other people's profile folders. On Linux it runs as a user named dokkit, which is made if useradd is there, and it reads only the folders that user can read. It may restart only the services or units that this machine's own configuration names, and only where the machine lets its account: on Windows the service's own permissions, on Linux root or systemd. Needs an administrator prompt on Windows and root on Linux. On Linux, run through sudo, it uses the enrolment of the account that ran sudo, and root's own when that account has none, and says which file it used. update puts this copy in place of the installed one and restarts the service. uninstall leaves the machine enrolled on the server.


## Tasks


### `dokkit task list`

The tasks on this machine and whether each is accepted. Lists the tasks in this folder and in the folders this machine reads. When the server answers, says of each whether it is accepted, not accepted yet, or changed since it was accepted. When it lists any tasks, says which account you are running as.


### `dokkit task run <name>`

Runs a task here to try it. Runs the task on this machine now. The server can only ask for a task a person accepted, pinned to the exact command accepted.


## Trying it with no server

```
$ dokkit check
dokkit.toml: upload-portal, 2 check(s)
  ok   http           http://localhost:8080/healthz
       would send {"at":"2026-10-06T22:08:58.1420895Z","check":"http","service":"upload-portal","state":"ok","type":"state","value":10}
  ok   tcp            port 5432
       would send {"at":"2026-10-06T22:08:58.1432929Z","check":"tcp","service":"upload-portal","state":"ok","type":"state","value":1}
```


# The Dokkit API

Dokkit watches machines, services and jobs. This is the HTTP API that the `dokkit` program, the command line, the client libraries, the MCP server and any script use.

Every call carries a key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Key prefixes: `dke_` enrolment token, `dkm_` machine key, `dka_` app key (write only), `dku_` user token with the scopes `read`, `read-logs`, `act`, `admin`.


## Intake

Machines and apps send reports, deploys and declarations. Machine key or app key.


### POST /api/v1/enrol

Trade an enrolment token for a machine key. Spends a one-use enrolment token and makes the machine. The answer holds the machine key, shown once. A name that is already enrolled answers 409 and the token is kept, unless the token was made for that machine; then it enrols again and revokes that machine's earlier keys. Takes no key in the header. The enrolment token (`dke_`) goes in the body.


Send:

```
{
  "token": "dke_3kQ9xV2mTn7LwRb8",
  "hostname": "db-01",
  "os": "windows",
  "arch": "amd64",
  "dokkit": "0.1.0"
}
```

`200` The machine and its key.

```json
{
  "machine": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
  "key": "dkm_7Hq2pXz4Yc9VnB1a"
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`409` Conflict.

`422` The body does not fit.

### POST /api/v1/report

Send a batch of lines. The main door. The body is newline-delimited JSON, one item per line, with a `type` and an `at` or `t`. The types are `state`, `inventory`, `metric`, `beat`, `job`, `stats`, `log`, `deploy` and `custom`. A batch is at most 5 MB compressed and 10,000 lines. A refused line does not fail the batch. Send the same `Dokkit-Batch` id again and nothing is stored twice. An app key may not send `state` or `inventory`, and may make 100 checks per service. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`) or an app key (`dka_`).

- `Dokkit-Batch` (header, optional): Names the batch. Sending it again stores nothing twice.
- `Content-Encoding` (header, optional): Set to gzip when the body is compressed.

Send:

```
{"type":"job","service":"nightly-purge","name":"nightly-purge","run":"r-2041","event":"ok","exit_code":0,"duration_ms":81234}
{"type":"log","t":"2026-10-05T21:14:03.120Z","level":"error","msg":"Upload failed","service":"upload-portal","fields":{"route":"/upload","status":500}}

```

`200` How many lines were accepted, and the ones refused.

```json
{
  "accepted": 1,
  "refused": [
    {
      "line": 2,
      "code": "unknown_service",
      "message": "No service \"upload-portal\" on this machine."
    }
  ]
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`413` Too large.

`422` The batch id is not a UUID (`bad_batch`), or the body is not valid gzip (`bad_gzip`).

`429` An app key has used up its bucket of 10,000 lines, refilling at 100 a second. Wait for Retry-After seconds.

### GET /api/v1/in/{key}/job/{name}/{event}

Ping a job with a web request. For anything that can only make a web request, such as a cron job on a storage box. `start`, `ok` and `fail` record the run. Any other event answers 404. Takes an app key (`dka_`).

- `key` (path): An app key (`dka_`). It travels in the address because the callers can only make a web request.
- `name` (path): The job's name.
- `event` (path): What happened.
- `run` (query, optional): Ties a start to its finish.

`200` Recorded.

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`404` Not found.

`413` Too large.

`422` The body does not fit.

`429` An app key has used up its bucket of 10,000 lines, refilling at 100 a second. Wait for Retry-After seconds.

### POST /api/v1/in/{key}/job/{name}/{event}

Ping a job and keep its output. Same as the GET. The body, if there is one, is kept as the last lines of the job's output, at most 16 KB. Any content type is accepted. Takes an app key (`dka_`).

- `key` (path): An app key (`dka_`). It travels in the address because the callers can only make a web request.
- `name` (path): The job's name.
- `event` (path): What happened.
- `run` (query, optional): Ties a start to its finish.

Send:

```
Purged 412 files.
Done.

```

`200` Recorded.

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`404` Not found.

`413` Too large.

`422` The body does not fit.

`429` An app key has used up its bucket of 10,000 lines, refilling at 100 a second. Wait for Retry-After seconds.

### PUT /api/v1/declare

Declare a service from a dokkit.toml. The contents of a `dokkit.toml`, sent as JSON with the same structure. Sending the same file twice changes nothing. Checks, jobs, logs and stats become active. Tasks become proposals. The file owns the service and its checks, so checks it no longer lists are removed. Only a machine key may declare; an app key answers 403. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`).


Send:

```
{
  "schema": 1,
  "service": {
    "id": "upload-portal",
    "name": "Upload portal",
    "kind": "service"
  },
  "check": [
    {
      "type": "http",
      "name": "front-page",
      "url": "http://localhost:8080/health",
      "expect": 200
    }
  ]
}
```

`200` The service id.

```json
{
  "service": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3"
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`422` The body does not fit.

### GET /api/v1/ping

Check the address, the key and the clock. Lets a machine check its address, its key and its clock. The answer holds the server's time. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`) or an app key (`dka_`).


`200` The key works.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "time": "2026-10-05T21:14:03.120000Z"
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

### POST /api/v1/proposals

Send what a scan found. What `dokkit scan` found, as the file was written. Nothing in it is active until a person accepts it in the interface. So far the server keeps running Windows services and listening ports, and leaves out what is already watched or was dismissed. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`).


Send:

```
{
  "os": "windows",
  "found": {
    "services": [
      {
        "name": "Spooler",
        "display": "Print Spooler",
        "state": "running"
      }
    ],
    "ports": [
      {
        "port": 5432,
        "program": "postgres.exe"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

`200` How many things from this machine now wait.

```json
{
  "waiting": 2
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`422` The body does not fit.

### POST /api/v1/deploys

Record a deploy from CI. For CI. `host` is the machine the version went onto, when that is not the machine the service lives on. A deploy is also recorded when a service's reported version changes, so most apps never call this. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`) or an app key (`dka_`).


Send:

```
{
  "service": "upload-portal",
  "version": "2.3.0",
  "host": "web-02",
  "commit": "abc123",
  "by": "ci"
}
```

`200` Recorded.

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`422` The body does not fit.

`429` An app key has used up its bucket of 10,000 lines, refilling at 100 a second. Wait for Retry-After seconds.

### GET /api/v1/checks

Get the checks added in the interface. The checks added in the interface for this machine, for the `dokkit` program to run. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`).


`200` The checks.

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "service": "spooler",
      "name": "windows-service",
      "type": "windows-service",
      "config": {
        "name": "Spooler"
      },
      "restart": false
    }
  ]
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

## Errors

Error reports from an app, in Dokkit's own format or as Sentry envelopes. App key.


### POST /api/v1/errors

Report an error in Dokkit's format. One error report. Reports are grouped by `type` and the app's own frames. Message text is dropped unless the service's page is set to keep it. An error does not open an issue or alert anyone. See `errors.md`. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`) or an app key (`dka_`).


Send:

```
{
  "at": "2026-10-05T21:14:03.120Z",
  "service": "upload-portal",
  "release": "2.3.0",
  "environment": "production",
  "host": "web-02",
  "type": "TimeoutError",
  "handled": true,
  "frames": [
    {
      "file": "app/worker.py",
      "function": "run_job",
      "line": 212,
      "own": true
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "route": "/upload",
    "status": "500"
  }
}
```

`200` Recorded.

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`422` The body does not fit.

`429` An app key has used up its bucket of 10,000 lines, refilling at 100 a second. Wait for Retry-After seconds.

### POST /api/{project}/envelope

Report errors from a Sentry SDK. The door for Sentry's open-source SDKs. An SDK is given an address made from an app key and Dokkit's host. Error events are stored; everything else is read and dropped, and the answer tells the SDK to stop sending those kinds. Gzip is accepted. The app key is read from the `X-Sentry-Auth` header, the `sentry_key` query value, or the envelope's first line. The `project` segment is whatever the SDK was given and is not used. Takes an app key (`dka_`).

- `project` (path): The project part of the address the SDK built.
- `sentry_key` (query, optional): The app key, when the SDK sends it in the query.
- `X-Sentry-Auth` (header, optional): Holds `sentry_key=<app key>` among its fields.
- `Content-Encoding` (header, optional): Set to gzip when the body is compressed.

Send:

```
{"event_id":"9ec79c33ec9942ab8353589fcb2e04dc","dsn":"https://dka_4Rm8@your.domain.com/1"}
{"type":"event"}
{"exception":{"values":[{"type":"TimeoutError","value":"upload timed out"}]},"release":"2.3.0"}

```

`200` Accepted. The `X-Sentry-Rate-Limits` header tells the SDK to stop sending kinds Dokkit drops.

```json
{}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`413` Too large.

`422` The body does not fit.

`429` An app key has used up its bucket of 10,000 lines, refilling at 100 a second. Wait for Retry-After seconds.

## Work

The `dokkit` program asks for tasks, sends their output and result, and fetches updates. Machine key.


### GET /api/v1/program/{target}

Download the newer dokkit program. The newer `dokkit` program this server holds, for a machine asked to fetch it. The target is the operating system and architecture, such as `windows-amd64`. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`).

- `target` (path): The kind of machine, as `<os>-<arch>`.

`200` The program file.

`401` Missing or bad key.

`404` Not found.

### GET /api/v1/work

Ask for a task to run. The `dokkit` program asks for work and the server holds the request for up to `wait` seconds. 204 means nothing to do; ask again. `command_sha256` is the pin of the task that was accepted; the program runs the task only when its own pin is the same one. A task has a name and nothing else. There are no arguments. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`).

- `wait` (query, optional): Seconds to hold the request.

`200` A task to run.

```json
{
  "run": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
  "task": "nightly-purge",
  "as": "ordinary",
  "command_sha256": "9f2b6c0d1e7a4b83a5c6f1d2e3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d1e0f9a8b7c6d5e4f30"
}
```

`204` Nothing to do. Ask again.

`401` Missing or bad key.

### POST /api/v1/work/{run}/output

Send a chunk of task output. A chunk of the running task's output, as plain text. The server keeps the last part. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`).

- `run` (path): The run id from `GET /work`.

Send:

```
Purged 412 files.

```

`200` Kept.

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`404` Not found.

### POST /api/v1/work/{run}/result

Send the result of a task. Either an exit code with the duration, or a refusal with the reason. A refusal is how the program says it will not run a task that is not defined on its machine or not accepted. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`).

- `run` (path): The run id from `GET /work`.

Send:

```
{
  "exit_code": 0,
  "duration_ms": 81234
}
```

`200` Kept.

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`404` The run is not running on this machine, or the body is neither an exit code nor a refusal.

### GET /api/v1/tasks/accepted

List the tasks accepted for this machine. So `dokkit task list` can say which tasks are accepted. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`).


`200` The accepted tasks.

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "task": "nightly-purge",
      "command_sha256": "9f2b6c0d1e7a4b83a5c6f1d2e3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d1e0f9a8b7c6d5e4f30",
      "as": "ordinary"
    }
  ]
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

## Read

Read issues, machines, services, jobs, logs, errors, deploys, rules, proposals and tasks. User token.


### GET /api/v1/proposals

List things waiting to be accepted. Found things and tasks that wait for a person to accept them. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `read` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


`200` OK.

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
      "kind": "service",
      "name": "Spooler",
      "detail": {
        "label": "Print Spooler",
        "saw": "Running"
      },
      "machine": "db-01"
    }
  ],
  "next": null
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

### GET /api/v1/deploys

List deploys. Deploy history, newest first. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `read` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


`200` OK.

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "service": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
      "name": "Upload portal",
      "machine": "web-02",
      "version": "2.3.0",
      "from": "2.2.9",
      "commit": "abc123",
      "by": "ci",
      "how": "reported",
      "at": "2026-10-05T19:30:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "next": null
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

### GET /api/v1/errors

List error groups. Error groups by type and place, newest first, at most 200. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `read` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


`200` OK.

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
      "type": "TimeoutError",
      "top": {
        "file": "app/worker.py",
        "function": "run_job",
        "line": 212,
        "own": true
      },
      "count": 14,
      "first_seen": "2026-10-05T19:40:00Z",
      "last_seen": "2026-10-05T21:14:03Z",
      "release": "2.3.0",
      "host": "web-02",
      "handled": true,
      "service": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
      "name": "Upload portal",
      "machine": "web-02"
    }
  ],
  "next": null
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

### GET /api/v1/day

The last day. The last 24 hours in 48 half hours, for each machine, and the issues that opened in that time. The last cell is the half hour that holds `to`. A cell is `down` if an issue that was down overlapped it, else `degraded` if any issue overlapped it, else `quiet` if the machine was heard from, else `none` (no signal). An issue counts in the state it has now, for its whole life. Soon issues and issues of services that are not in production colour nothing. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `read` scope.

- `to` (query, optional): The end of the window, RFC 3339. Defaults to now.

`200` OK.

### GET /api/v1/inbox

What needs a look. What needs a look, what will soon, what was found and is not watched, what is snoozed, issues in other environments, and how many things are fine. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `read` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


`200` OK.

```json
{
  "needs_you": [
    {
      "id": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
      "short_id": "DOK-12",
      "kind": "check",
      "state": "down",
      "title": "upload-portal is down",
      "note": "Connection refused",
      "count": 3,
      "since": "2026-10-05T20:41:00Z",
      "snoozed_until": null,
      "acknowledged_at": null,
      "machine": "web-02",
      "service": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
      "alert": {
        "channel": "page",
        "status": "sent"
      },
      "soon": false
    }
  ],
  "soon": [
    {
      "id": "9b2e4d10-77aa-4c3e-8f61-2a5c0d9e1b44",
      "short_id": "DOK-13",
      "kind": "check",
      "state": "degraded",
      "title": "Certificate for upload-portal expires in 12 days",
      "note": "12 days left",
      "count": 1,
      "since": "2026-10-05T20:41:00Z",
      "snoozed_until": null,
      "acknowledged_at": null,
      "machine": "web-02",
      "service": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
      "alert": {
        "channel": "push",
        "status": "sent"
      },
      "soon": true
    }
  ],
  "not_watched": [
    {
      "id": "c1d7a0f2-5e3b-4a96-b8d4-0f7e2a6c9b15",
      "kind": "port",
      "name": "5432",
      "detail": {
        "label": "Port 5432",
        "saw": "postgres"
      },
      "machine": "db-01"
    }
  ],
  "snoozed": [],
  "other_environments": [
    {
      "environment": "dev",
      "issues": []
    }
  ],
  "fine": {
    "services": 14,
    "machines": 5
  }
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`200` OK.

```json
{
  "items": [

      "alert": {
        "channel": "page",
        "status": "sent"
      }
    }
  ],
  "next": null
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

### GET /api/v1/issues/{id}

- `id` (path): The id of the issue.

`200` OK.

```json
{
  "id": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
  "short_id": "DOK-12",

  },
  "closed_at": null,

      "text": "Restarted the pool.",
```

### GET /api/v1/services

### GET /api/v1/services/{id}

Get one service. One service with its checks, facts, routing, version and open issue. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `read` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.

- `id` (path): The id of the service.

`200` OK.

```json
{
  "id": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
```

### GET /api/v1/services/{id}/series

Get chart data for a service. Without `metric`, the names of the metrics the service has. With `metric`, its points between `from` and `to`. Answers 404 for an unknown service, a time that is not RFC 3339, or a `from` that is not before `to`. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `read` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.

- `id` (path): The id of the service.
- `metric` (query, optional): The metric's name.
- `from` (query, optional): Start, RFC 3339. Defaults to 24 hours before `to`.
- `to` (query, optional): End, RFC 3339. Defaults to now.
- `points` (query, optional): How many points.

`200` OK.

```json
{
  "metric": "queue_depth",
  "points": [
    {
      "at": "2026-10-05T20:00:00Z",
      "value": 4
    }
  ]
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`404` Not found.

### GET /api/v1/jobs

List jobs. Every job with its schedule, last run, last good run and next expected run. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `read` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


`200` OK.

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
      "name": "nightly-purge",
      "machine": "nas",
      "state": "ok",
      "schedule": "0 2 * * *",
      "last_run": {
        "run": "r-2041",
        "result": "ok",
        "started_at": "2026-10-05T02:00:01Z",
        "finished_at": "2026-10-05T02:01:22Z",
        "exit_code": 0,
        "duration_ms": 81234,
        "tail": "Purged 412 files."
      },
      "last_good_run": null,
      "next_expected": "2026-10-06T02:00:00Z",
      "grace": "30m",
      "max_runtime": null
    }
  ],
  "next": null
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

### GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/runs

List the runs of a job. The recent runs of one job, up to 100. The id is the job's service id. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `read` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.

- `id` (path): The id of the job's service.

`200` OK.

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "run": "r-2041",
      "result": "ok",
      "started_at": "2026-10-05T02:00:01Z",
      "finished_at": "2026-10-05T02:01:22Z",
      "exit_code": 0,
      "duration_ms": 81234,
      "tail": "Purged 412 files."
    }
  ],
  "next": null
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`404` Not found.

### GET /api/v1/logs

Search log lines. Log lines, newest first, at most 500. `level` is that level and worse. Answers 404 for an unknown machine or service, or a time that is not RFC 3339. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `read-logs` scope.

- `q` (query, optional): Search text.
- `level` (query, optional): That level and worse.
- `machine` (query, optional): A machine id or name.
- `service` (query, optional): A service id.
- `from` (query, optional): Start, RFC 3339.
- `to` (query, optional): End, RFC 3339.

`200` OK.

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "t": "2026-10-05T21:14:03.120Z",
      "level": "error",
      "msg": "Upload failed",
      "fields": {
        "route": "/upload",
        "status": 500
      },
      "machine": "web-02",
      "service": "upload-portal"
    }
  ],
  "next": null
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`404` Not found.

## Act

Snooze and acknowledge issues, route and hold services, accept found things, run tasks, keep error text and set when a job is late. User token with `act`.


### POST /api/v1/issues/{id}/snooze

Snooze an issue. Snoozes an issue until a time. An unknown issue answers 404. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `act` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.

- `id` (path): The id of the issue.

Send:

```
{
  "until": "2026-10-06T08:00:00Z"
}
```

`200` Done.

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`404` Not found.

`422` The body does not fit.

### PUT /api/v1/services/{id}/routing

Set who is told about a service. Sets the channel for `down` and for `degraded`. A field that is not sent stays as it was; a value that is not a channel clears that route. `night` is optional; false holds the alerts of a night until it ends. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `act` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.

- `id` (path): The id of the service.

```
  "night": false
}
```

```json
  "machine": "nas",
  "channel": "page",
  "on": true
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`404` Not found.

### DELETE /api/v1/rules/{id}

Delete an alert rule. Deletes a rule. Deleting one that is not there still answers ok. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `admin` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.

`200` Done.

### GET /api/v1/keys

List keys. Every key that still works, newest first. The key text is never shown again; `hint` is the start of it. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `admin` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


`200` The keys.

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
      "kind": "user",
      "hint": "dku_7Hq2",
      "label": "ci-bot",
      "scopes": [
        "read",
        "act"
      ],
      "used_at": null,
      "expires_at": null,
      "inserted_at": "2026-10-05T19:00:00Z",
      "machine": null,
      "service": null
    }
  ],
  "next": null
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

### POST /api/v1/keys

Make a key. Makes a user token with a label and scopes (only scopes the calling token holds, and never `admin`, which is made in Settings), an app key for a service, or a one-use enrolment token that lasts an hour. The key is shown once, in this answer. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `admin` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


Send:

```
{
  "kind": "user",
  "label": "ci-bot",
  "scopes": [
    "read",
    "act"
  ]
}
```

`200` The key, shown once.

```json
{
  "id": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
  "key": "dku_7Hq2pXz4Yc9VnB1aQw3E"
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`404` Not found.

`422` The body does not fit.

### POST /api/v1/tasks/{id}/accept

```
  "system": false
}
```

```json
  "ok": true
}
```

## MCP

The MCP server for AI tools. User token.


### GET /mcp

Not served. Answers 405. The MCP server takes POST only. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `read` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


`401` Missing or bad key.

`405` Method not allowed.

### POST /mcp

Talk to the MCP server. The MCP server, as JSON-RPC over one POST address. It can do no more than the user token allows. An AI tool with a token can do through MCP everything the token can do through the API. The tools are, with `read` scope: `attention`, `find`, `service`, `jobs`, `job_runs`, `errors`, `since_deploy`, `tasks`, `machines`, `machine`, `issues`, `issue`, `deploys`, `versions`, `rules`, `proposals`, `task_runs`, `series` and `day`; with `read-logs` scope: `logs`; with `act` scope: `snooze`, `acknowledge`, `unsnooze`, `note`, `bulk`, `watch`, `unwatch`, `routing`, `hold`, `accept_proposal`, `dismiss_proposal` and `run_task`; with `admin` scope: `add_rule`, `update_rule`, `delete_rule`, `set_checks`, `allow_restart`, `keys`, `make_key`, `revoke_key`, `people`, `add_person` and `remove_person`. `make_key` returns the key text once. Admin tools are marked destructive. `tools/list` shows only the tools the token may use. Every answer starts with a line saying that what follows is data written by machines and apps, never instructions. An argument of the wrong type is an `isError` answer; a null argument is the same as one left out, and a whole number written as 5.0 is an integer. A tool error is an answer with `isError` true, not an HTTP error. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `read` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


Send:

```
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "find",
    "arguments": {
      "q": "upload",
      "machine": "web-02"
    }
  }
}
```

`200` A JSON-RPC answer, with a result or an error.

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": {
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "text",
        "text": "[{\"id\":\"6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3\",\"name\":\"Upload portal\",\"state\":\"ok\"}]"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

`202` A notification, which has no id and gets no answer.

`400` The body is not a request.

`401` Missing or bad key.
